newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil cargo trades steady, barges quiet.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil cargo trades steady, barges quiet.

text.p: European gas oil differentials were little changed on Thursday, with barge sellers struggling to find buyers and cargoes trading steadily at stable prices.
August IPE gas oil was 25 cents firmer at $165.25 a tonnes at 1115 GMT, moving in a tight range along with Brent.

A cargo of German heating oil moved at August IPE +$1.25, around unchnaged, for August delivery. Later talk put the bid at +$0.50 and offer at +$2. A pipeline heating oil delivery was also agreed for inland UK but the value was not known.
A 20,000 flexi cargo of EN590 low sulphur diesel moved into France on Wednesday at August IPE +$5.25, slightly firmer.
EN590 into Germany was talked around August IPE +$2.50/ $3.00. On Thursday EN590 into France for first half August was talked at August IPE +$4.25/$5.25.
Barges were almost dormant, depressed by continuing dollar strength. The dollar was higher at 1.8286 marks at 1105 GMT.
One trader reported moving a 1,000 tonne parcel of prompt Rotterdam refinery heating oil at August +$0.75, a strong number compared to the talked value of August IPE flat to 50 cents.
Traders predicted the market would revive when Iraqi oil exports resume and the outright crude price falls.
